per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a WARC record

retention.stated: one index per crawl, all still listed: collinfo.json names 129 crawl indexes, from CC-MAIN-2008-2009 to CC-MAIN-2026-43

egress.terms: No charge and no account for HTTPS downloads of the data and index files from data.commoncrawl.org.

interface_detail: Index API per crawl on index.commoncrawl.org; WARC files on data.commoncrawl.org
tooling: Any HTTP client: a CDXJ lookup on index.commoncrawl.org returns a WARC filename, offset and length, and a byte-range GET on data.commoncrawl.org returns that one record.
chaining: A CDXJ lookup on index.commoncrawl.org names the WARC file, offset and length of a stored capture and one byte-range GET on data.commoncrawl.org reads it, so a page Common Crawl captured is read from the crawl copy when a live fetch fails; for broad or large-scale URL filtering Common Crawl points callers to its URL Index (formerly the Columnar Index) through Amazon Athena or Apache Spark instead of the CDXJ API

limits.value: at most 1 request a second (HTTP level) on index.commoncrawl.org: the rate a Common Crawl engineer asked index callers to keep to on the Common Crawl user forum in April 2023

no concurrent requests from one IP address on the CDXJ API: callers are asked to sleep between calls, not to run multiple threads at once on the same IP and not to use proxy networks; an HTTP 503 answer means the acceptable request rate is exceeded
the CDXJ API on index.commoncrawl.org is heavily rate limited; an IP address that sends too many requests may be blocked, and a blocked IP address should wait 24 hours

reliability_note: The CDXJ index is intermittent: on 2026-10-30 the same lookup answered 504 Gateway Time-out from nginx after 11.0 s and 200 after 9.1 s, while a WARC byte-range read on data.commoncrawl.org answered 206 in 0.7 s.
